original_test_intent: Physically inspect and cycle the specified OSFP module, confirm correct seating and cage/latch condition, and verify after the approved reboot or port reinitialization that the same module/port is detected and operates without new errors.
original_method: A trained operator binds module serial/part number to cage/port, records pre-state photos and module/link inventory, establishes ESD/optical and required power/link isolation, removes/reinserts the module once using the service procedure, restores latch/cable/dust protection, then compares EEPROM/DOM, link/driver and error evidence after approved recovery.
manual_activity: A trained operator physically inspects, removes and reseats the exact OSFP module under ESD/optical/service controls and verifies cage/latch/cable state; the owner reviews physical and link evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/switch, exact OSFP part/serial/firmware and cage/port/lane/cable identity
Approved module service procedure, cycle count, hot-plug/power/link isolation and optical safety requirements
Pre/post EEPROM/DOM or module inventory, link/driver and error acceptance criteria
Independent console/network recovery and spare module/port escalation path
Camera/evidence labeling, operator identity and no-log-clear policy
safety_requirements: Only a trained operator may handle the OSFP under approved ESD and optical safety controls
Do not view exposed optics or manipulate a live optical/link path outside the vendor procedure
Stop on wrong module/port, damaged cage/latch/contacts, contamination, excessive force, optical hazard, link/boot failure or new error
Perform one approved cycle only and diagnose before any repeat
Restore latch, cable, dust-cover and approved final port state
agent_execution_scope: Verify row-2004 variant identity and prepare the OSFP module/cage evidence checklist
Collect and compare pre/post module EEPROM/DOM or inventory, firmware, port/link/driver state and unfiltered errors
Organize photos, action/recovery timeline and evidence hashes
Flag changed module identity, missing detection, lane/link degradation or incomplete physical proof
Perform no physical/optical manipulation, seating verdict, reinitialization authorization or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact module/cage/port, safe service sequence, cycle count and recovery plan
Ensure trained operator completes physical inspection/reseat and signs the evidence
Review physical, module telemetry and link/error changes and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The NO decision is correct because remote commands cannot seat/unseat or visually inspect an OSFP. They can only corroborate module identity, DOM, link and errors around the operator action.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use project-approved read-only module EEPROM/DOM, port inventory, lane/link, driver and log commands before and after the operator's one physical cycle; commands depend on the switch/NIC package.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: OSFP Module scope, plug/unplug and post-cycle detection intent, seating criterion and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL MANUAL PHYSICAL OSFP MODULE RESEAT VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed module/cage checklist and before/after photos keyed to serial/port, with ESD/optical/safe-state confirmation, one-cycle timeline and correlated EEPROM/DOM, link/lane/driver and error evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds OSFP-specific optical, cage, identity and link recovery controls without automating the essential physical judgment.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Remote module detection cannot prove latch, contact, keying or cage condition; physical inspection and complete link/module evidence are both required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A cycle can contaminate optics, damage high-density contacts or interrupt fabric connectivity. A link-up result may still hide degraded lanes or incomplete latch engagement.

project_override_considerations: If the OSFP is approved for live hot-plug, the exact optical/link drain and service sequence must be supplied; otherwise isolate/power down as required. Do not borrow BF3 cable criteria from row 2007.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash plus OSFP part/serial/firmware, cage/port/lane/cable and service-procedure revision
Operator identity, ESD/optical/safe-state confirmation and labeled before/after cage/module photos
Pre/post EEPROM/DOM or module inventory, port/lane/link/driver state, recovery timeline and unfiltered errors
One-cycle/no-repeat/no-log-clear audit, restored latch/cable/final state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently targets OSFP module physical cycling, detection and seating. The shared code is an identity hazard, but row 2004 and its hash uniquely select this module variant.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case is MANUAL ONLY rather than globally blocked. Physical access, trained operator, service procedure and recovery controls are prerequisites while static review is complete.

review_improvement: Binds the shared code to the OSFP module variant and adds cage/contact, optical safety, module identity and lane/link evidence to the one-cycle workflow.
independent_technical_reasoning: An OSFP can enumerate while mechanically marginal, and a simple link-up can mask lane degradation or a compromised latch/contact. Conversely, loss of link after the cycle must be tied to the exact module, port and cable path. Physical cage/latch inspection and module/lane telemetry therefore cover different failure modes. The shared-code BF3 cable case is excluded because cable mating and module seating have different identities, hazards and criteria.
